questions.def: We use 'do' as an auxiliary verb for emphasis.
questions.question: I did ___ my homework!

questions.def: 'Did' emphasizes the action of saying sorry.
questions.question: He ___ say he was sorry!

questions.def: 'Do want' emphasizes the desire for a new bike.
questions.question: I ___ a new bike!

questions.def: 'Do' emphasizes the state of looking tired.
questions.question: You ___ look tired!

questions.def: 'Do' emphasizes that they like pizza.
questions.question: They ___ like pizza.

questions.def: 'Do love' emphasizes the feeling of loving the game.
questions.question: We ___ this game!

questions.def: 'Does' emphasizes that he cares.
questions.question: He ___ care about you.

questions.def: 'Do' emphasizes the need for help.
questions.question: I ___ need your help!

questions.def: 'Do believe' emphasizes the act of believing.
questions.question: I ___ you!

questions.def: 'Do' emphasizes that they understand.
questions.question: They ___ understand the problem.

questions.def: 'Do' emphasizes the act of remembering.
questions.question: We ___ remember you!

questions.def: 'Do hope' emphasizes the hope that they can come.
questions.question: I ___ you can come!

questions.def: 'Does' emphasizes her knowledge of the answer.
questions.question: She ___ know the answer.

questions.def: 'Do' emphasizes how beautiful you look.
questions.question: You ___ look beautiful!

questions.def: 'Does' is for third-person singular, not 'I'.
questions.question: I does believe in magic.

questions.def: 'Do think' emphasizes that I think it's a good idea.
questions.question: I ___ it's a good idea.

questions.def: 'Do' emphasizes their enjoyment of playing games.
questions.question: They ___ enjoy playing games.

questions.def: 'Does' emphasizes that he understands.
questions.question: He ___ understand what you mean!

questions.def: Use 'does' for third-person singular.
questions.question: She do wants to go.

questions.def: 'Do agree' emphasizes the agreement.
questions.question: I ___ with you.

questions.def: 'Do' emphasizes that we appreciate the help.
questions.question: We ___ appreciate your help.

questions.def: 'Does' emphasizes that she tries her best.
questions.question: She ___ try her best!

questions.def: Use 'do' for plural subjects like 'they'.
questions.question: They does know how to cook.

questions.def: 'Do hope' emphasizes the desire to see them again.
questions.question: We ___ to see you again soon.

questions.def: 'Do' emphasizes the act of remembering.
questions.question: I ___ remember meeting him.

questions.def: 'Does' emphasizes the need for a vacation.
questions.question: She ___ need a vacation!

questions.def: Use 'does' for third person singular subjects.
questions.question: He do wants to help.

questions.def: Use 'really' after 'do/does/did' to add emphasis.
questions.question: I do ___ want to go to the party!

questions.def: After 'it was/is', use the subject pronoun (he/she/I/we/they).
questions.question: It was ___ who broke the vase!

questions.def: Use 'do/does/did + believe' to show disbelief or surprise.
questions.question: I ___ saw a ghost!
